events_chronological: The assassin code-named Mantis leaves the Adder Unit for the child she is carrying and plans a wedding in a desert chapel under a new name.
Corvin and the rest of the unit walk into the wedding rehearsal and massacre everyone in the chapel.
Corvin shoots Mantis through the head, and she survives in a coma.
Reiko Sana, whose parents were murdered in front of her as a child, kills the boss responsible at eleven and grows up to be a top assassin.
Reiko takes the eastern capital's underworld by beheading a rival at a council meeting, and rules it with the schoolgirl killer Momo and the lawyer Delphine.
The one-eyed Dara comes to the hospital to kill the comatose Mantis with a syringe and is called off by Corvin at the last moment.
For four years an orderly called Wade sells the comatose woman's body to visitors.
Mantis wakes, kills Wade and his customer, and finds her belly flat and her baby gone.
She lies in the back of Wade's truck for thirteen hours until she can move her toes.
Mantis writes out her list of five names and drives to Odette Bray's house in the suburbs.
The two fight through the kitchen, break off when Odette's small daughter comes home from school, and Mantis kills Odette with a thrown knife in front of the child.
Mantis flies to a southern island and talks the retired swordsmith Ito into making her a blade to kill his own former student, Corvin.
In the eastern capital Mantis cuts Delphine's arm off outside a restaurant called the Lantern and sends her to Corvin as a message.
Mantis kills Momo and then fights her way through the Eighty across the restaurant.
Mantis duels Reiko in the snow garden and takes off the top of her skull.
She interrogates the maimed Delphine in the boot of a car and leaves her alive to tell Corvin everything.
Corvin asks Delphine whether Mantis knows that her daughter is still alive.
nonlinear_category_reason: Numbered chapters, each built around one name on the list, with a target's backstory delivered when she appears rather than when it happened.
syuzhet_notes: The film is cut into numbered chapters that ignore chronology outright. Told-order bullet 1 is the shooting everything hangs on, played before anything that explains it; bullet 2 opens the first chapter with what is chronologically the second-to-last killing on the list; and bullets 4-9 then reach back to the massacre and the four-year coma. Told-order bullets 10-11 are an animated flashback covering one antagonist's entire life, dropped in immediately before she dies.
fabula_notes: The massacre at the chapel is shown only in fragments - a black-and-white aftermath and a few seconds of the rehearsal - so the events leading up to it are partly inferred. That the child survived is withheld until the last line, which retroactively changes the meaning of the waking scene.
